verdict.reasoning: REFUTED - formatting-only, no content discrepancy. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. The heading is present at line 13688, verbatim and complete, with its correct clause number, its correct title, and its anchor ''. The kind label 'missing-heading' misdescribes the observation; the claim is about the '#' count, not about absent text. Page 314's body is likewise complete against the render: the NOTE, 12.3.5.1 General, 12.3.5.2 General format ('SOURCE-COMPUTER. [ computer-name-1 ] .' with SOURCE-COMPUTER underlined), 12.3.5.3 Syntax rule 1), and 12.3.5.4 General rules 1)-3) all match the PDF word for word. (2) THE PDF HAS NO HEADING RANK TO LOSE. I rendered page 314 and page 313 at 300 dpi and cropped/zoomed the heading band. '12.3.5 SOURCE-COMPUTER paragraph' and '12.3.5.1 General' are printed in the SAME bold serif at the SAME size; on page 313, '12.3 Configuration section', '12.3.1 General', '12.3.2 General format', '12.3.3 Syntax rules' and '12.3.4 General rule' are ALSO all printed in that same identical bold type. ISO gives these clause headings no typographic differentiation whatsoever - depth is encoded ONLY by the dotted clause number. The markdown preserves that number ('12.3.5') exactly, so the hierarchy the PDF actually asserts is fully and correctly transcribed. There is no PDF fact that the markdown contradicts. (3) THE '#' DEPTH IS A SYSTEMIC PAGE-LOCAL TRANSCRIPTION ARTIFACT, NOT A PAGE-314 DEFECT. Across the whole file, markdown level bears no consistent relation to clause depth: of 801 clause-depth-3 headings, 508 are '###', 276 are '##', and 17 are '####'; clause-depth-2 splits 162 '##' / 26 '###'; clause-depth-4 splits 162 '##' / 620 '###' / 24 '####'. Local siblings show the same churn - '## 12.3.6.4' is h2 while 12.3.6.1-.3 are h3; '## 12.3.7.2/.3/.4' are h2 while 12.3.7.1 is h3; '## 12.3.8.4' is h2 while 12.3.8.1-.3 are h3. The promoted headings are the ones that open a transcribed page (12.3.5 is the first heading on page 314), i.e. each page was levelled independently. (4) THE STATED HARM RESTS ON A FALSE PREMISE. 'Any outline built from heading levels' does not exist for this document and never did: the transcription emits the running header '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' as an h1 941 times and a '## Page NNN' marker as an h2 1261 times, interleaved throughout. That page scaffold shreds any level-derived outline document-wide, independent of 12.3.5. Nor is 12.3.5 uniquely orphaned relative to its parent: '## 12.3 Configuration section' is itself an h2 while its own siblings '### 12.1 General' and '### 12.2 Environment division structure' are h3, so the parent's level is equally arbitrary. Any consumer of this file must key on the clause number, which is intact. The claim's quotations of both sources are accurate, but the difference is pure markdown formatting, changes no meaning, loses no text, and contradicts nothing the PDF prints.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The heading '12.3.5 SOURCE-COMPUTER paragraph' is present, complete and correctly numbered at line 13688, and all of page 314's content matches the PDF exactly. The observation reduces to a markdown '##'-vs-'###' depth choice, which the PDF does not constrain - ISO prints 12.3, 12.3.1 and 12.3.5 in identical bold type and encodes hierarchy solely in the dotted clause number, which is transcribed verbatim. The uneven '#' depth is a document-wide, page-local levelling artifact (276 of 801 clause-depth-3 headings are h2, plus 941 h1 running headers and 1261 '## Page N' h2 markers), so it is at most a cosmetic normalization chore for the whole file, not a page-314 structural finding.
